references.context: Measure theory: given a measurable space (X,Σ), a subset A⊆X is called measurable exactly when A∈Σ. This is not all subsets of X unless Σ is the full power set, and does not presuppose a measure or probability function.

It is not an additional independently named mathematical prerequisite, and the source does not require individual events to have positive probability.
Probability is distinguished by normalization to unit total mass.

references.disposition: The equality of left and right cosets for every g∈G is exactly the defining normal-subgroup criterion in this formulation. The group, subgroup, and both left/right coset constructions are already independently linked. The statement is stronger than equality for one selected g and does not create a new independent coset-equality meaning.
Every subgroup has both coset families, but equality at every g is an additional condition.
